scenes.title: The Road Map of Market Breadth
scenes.concept: The Road Map of Market Breadth

beatOutlines.textOutline: According to John Murphy, market breadth measures internal market health.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second pillar is McClellan Oscillator and Summation Index for momentum cycles.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The third component is 52-week New Highs-Lows and Arms Index (TRIN).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And finally, Equivolume where bar width plots genuine volume pressure.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: The Road Map of Market Breadth

beatOutlines.textOutline: Every day in the market, a tug of war unfolds between advancing and declining stocks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When advances exceed declines, net advances are added to yesterday's cumulative line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: But when the index rises while declines dominate, market breadth hollows out.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: John Murphy writes: the AD Line often turns weeks or months ahead of price indices.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If index forms higher highs while AD line prints lower highs, it is bearish divergence.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Conversely at market bottoms, when AD Line turns up first, it signals massive accumulation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Marian and Sherman McClellan applied two exponential moving averages to net advances.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the oscillator reaches +100 or -100, the market reaches an extreme boundary.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And when we sum these daily oscillator values, we get the McClellan Summation Index.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Track the strongest 52-week Highs against the weakest 52-week Lows.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's rule: if New Lows begin climbing above 50, the rally is highly suspect.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When New Lows surpass New Highs, the broader market enters a definitive downtrend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Upside Volume vs Downside Volume & TRIN
scenes.concept: Upside Volume vs Downside Volume & TRIN

beatOutlines.textOutline: Counting stock numbers alone isn't enough; we must see where money is actually flowing.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Richard Arms combined advances and volume to develop the Arms Index (TRIN).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: TRIN is inverted. Below 1.0 is bullish, and above 2.0 indicates panic selling.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: Upside Volume vs Downside Volume & TRIN

beatOutlines.textOutline: Richard Arms invented Equivolume, where volume sits inside the bar rather than below.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A thin tall bar shows easy move on low volume; a wide box reveals massive institutional war.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In Candlepower, Japanese open-close candle bodies merge with Equivolume widths.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Analyze this scenario carefully and pick the correct answer.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think. The index is rising, but what warning do internal breadth and TRIN give?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Correct answer: This is classic Bearish Divergence masking severe heavy distribution.
